newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end narrowly mixed in rudderless trade.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end narrowly mixed in rudderless trade.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Monday in insipid trade with foreign investors absent due to the U.S. Veterans' Day holiday and local players uninspired to enter the market, brokers said.
The market was seen directionless this week as investor caution ahead of Wednesday's U.S. Federal Reserve meeting was likely to exacerbate a recent trend of low volumes, they said.
Monday, the General Index fell 0.15 percent to 1,498.0 points, and the blue-chip Selective Index rose 0.68 percent to 2,104.4 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
The blue chip rises were due to small local players hunting for bargains after the general downward trend of the last few weeks cheapened some stocks, brokers said.

"The market is still depressed," said Enrique Hernndez of local brokerage Macrovalores. "There is some selective buying of cheap stocks going on, but there is no money of any great significance coming in."
"Rather than entering Latin America, funds are staying in the United States as investors await a Fed announcement," said Hernando Pastor of local brokerage T&J.
Due to rules introduced on the market last week, stocks can continue to be traded, but their prices are fixed one hour before the end of the day's session.
Brokers and stock exchange officials have said the market's indices will only vary slightly in this final hour.
When prices were fixed Monday at 1700 local time/2200 GMT, there had been 1,226 trades in volume estimated at 13.0 million soles ($5.0 million), brokers said.
Benchmark Telefnica del Per was stable at 5.50 soles, on a preliminary count of 335,985 million shares.
Among other leaders, tin miner Minsur rose 1.13 percent to 23.26 soles on a preliminary share count of 89,376, while Banco de Crdito closed unchanged at 3.80 soles on preliminary volume of 51,527.
